connectorUiConfig.title: QCrypton PQC Scanner Agent
connectorUiConfig.descriptionMarkdown: The [QCrypton PQC Scanner Agent](https://www.qcrypton.com/) data connector ingests post-quantum cryptography readiness findings from internal network scans into Microsoft Sentinel through the QCrypton API. The Scanner Agent probes TLS posture on VNet-internal Azure endpoints and network appliances including F5 BIG-IP, Check Point, Palo Alto, Cisco ASA, and Fortinet FortiGate. Findings include quantum-vulnerable certificates, weak TLS configurations, classical key exchanges, and PQC readiness status.

| where Metadata contains '"source":"scanner-agent"' or ResourceType has_any ('F5', 'CheckPoint', 'PaloAlto', 'Cisco', 'Fortinet')

sampleQueries.description: All quantum-vulnerable internal findings in the last 24h
sampleQueries.query:
PQReadiness_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where QuantumPosture == 'vulnerable'
| where ResourceType has_any ('F5', 'CheckPoint', 'PaloAlto', 'Cisco', 'Fortinet', 'Azure/AppService', 'Azure/ContainerApp', 'Azure/FrontDoor', 'Azure/ApiManagement')
| project TimeGenerated, ResourceName, ResourceType, AssetKind, Algorithm, PostureReason, RiskScore
| order by RiskScore desc

instructionSteps.title: Connect QCrypton PQC Scanner Agent to Microsoft Sentinel

parameters.content: This connector polls the QCrypton PQC Scanner Agent API to retrieve post-quantum cryptography readiness findings from internal network scans and ingest them into the **PQReadiness_CL** table in your Log Analytics workspace.

#### 1. Deploy the Scanner Agent
Deploy the QCrypton PQC Scanner Agent as an Azure Container App in your VNet. Follow the [deployment guide](https://www.qcrypton.com/docs/scanner-agent) to configure appliance targets (F5 BIG-IP, Check Point, Palo Alto, Cisco, Fortinet) and Azure endpoint discovery.

#### 2. API Key
Obtain your QCrypton API key from the [QCrypton Portal](https://portal.qcrypton.com). Navigate to **Settings > API Keys** and generate a key with read access to agent scan findings.

#### 3. API Server URL
Enter the base URL of your QCrypton API server. The default is `https://api.qcrypton.com`. If you use a dedicated or regional instance, enter the URL provided by QCrypton.

parameters.label: QCrypton API Server URL
parameters.name: apiServerUrl
parameters.description: Enter the QCrypton API base URL. Do not include a trailing slash or path.

dataFlows.transformKql: source | extend TimeGenerated = iff(isnull(TimeGenerated), now(), TimeGenerated) | project TimeGenerated, ResourceId, ResourceType, ResourceName, SubscriptionId, ResourceGroup, Location, AssetKind, AssetIdentifier, Algorithm, KeySize, Curve, SignatureAlgorithm, QuantumPosture, PostureReason, RiskScore, ExpiresOn, Metadata

schema.name: PQReadiness_CL
schema.description: Post-quantum cryptography readiness findings from QCrypton PQC Scanner Agent. Contains scan results for internal network appliances (F5 BIG-IP, Check Point, Palo Alto, Cisco ASA, Fortinet), VNet-internal Azure endpoints, TLS certificate posture, and PQC readiness status.

columns.name: TimeGenerated
columns.description: Timestamp when the finding was generated by the scanner agent.

columns.name: ResourceId
columns.description: Azure Resource Manager resource ID of the scanned resource, or appliance identifier for network devices.

columns.name: ResourceType
columns.description: Resource type (e.g., F5/LTM, CheckPoint/Certificate, PaloAlto/Certificate, Cisco/Certificate, Fortinet/Certificate, Azure/AppService, Azure/ContainerApp).

columns.name: ResourceName
columns.description: Display name or hostname of the scanned resource or appliance.

columns.name: SubscriptionId
columns.description: Azure subscription ID containing the scanner agent deployment.

columns.name: ResourceGroup
columns.description: Resource group containing the scanned resource.

columns.name: Location
columns.description: Azure region of the scanned resource.

columns.name: AssetKind
columns.description: Classification of the cryptographic asset (tls-cert, tls-config).

columns.name: AssetIdentifier
columns.description: Unique identifier for the cryptographic asset (host:port).

columns.name: Algorithm
columns.description: Cryptographic algorithm in use (e.g., RSA, ECDSA, Ed25519, ML-DSA, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384).

columns.name: KeySize
columns.description: Key size in bits (e.g., 2048, 4096). 0 for non-key assets.

columns.name: Curve
columns.description: Elliptic curve name if applicable (e.g., P-256, P-384).

columns.name: SignatureAlgorithm
columns.description: Signature algorithm of the certificate (e.g., SHA256WithRSA, ECDSAWithSHA384).

columns.name: QuantumPosture
columns.description: Quantum readiness posture: vulnerable, partial, or compliant.

columns.name: PostureReason
columns.description: Human-readable explanation for the quantum posture classification.

columns.name: RiskScore
columns.description: Numeric risk score (0-30) reflecting quantum vulnerability severity.

columns.name: ExpiresOn
columns.description: Expiry date of the certificate. Null for non-certificate assets.

columns.name: Metadata
columns.description: JSON metadata: {scanId, rule, protocol}. Rule identifies the finding type (e.g., quantum_vulnerable_cert, f5_pqc_engine_active, checkpoint_cert_quantum_vulnerable).

properties.displayName: [parameters('workbook1-name')]

properties.description:
A network appliance (F5 BIG-IP, Check Point, Palo Alto, Cisco ASA, or Fortinet) is presenting a
TLS certificate signed with a classical algorithm (RSA/ECDSA) that is vulnerable to quantum attack.
These appliances terminate TLS for critical internal traffic and are prime harvest-now-decrypt-later
targets. Migrate to PQ-hybrid certificates or deploy QCrypton PQC Engine to front the appliance.
properties.displayName: Network appliance serving quantum-vulnerable certificate
properties.query:
PQReadiness_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where AssetKind == "tls-cert"
| where QuantumPosture == "vulnerable"
| where ResourceType has_any ("F5", "CheckPoint", "PaloAlto", "Cisco", "Fortinet")
| project TimeGenerated, ResourceName, ResourceType, AssetIdentifier, Algorithm, SignatureAlgorithm, KeySize, ExpiresOn, RiskScore, PostureReason, SubscriptionId, ResourceGroup
| order by RiskScore desc

properties.displayName: Network appliance serving quantum-vulnerable certificate

properties.description: InternalEndpointWeakTLS_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.0.0

A VNet-internal Azure endpoint or network appliance is accepting TLS below version 1.3. Only
TLS 1.3 supports negotiation of hybrid post-quantum key exchange groups (X25519MLKEM768). Internal
endpoints on legacy TLS cannot be upgraded to PQ without a protocol change. Upgrade the minimum
TLS version to 1.3 to enable PQC readiness.
properties.displayName: Internal endpoint using TLS protocol below 1.3
properties.query:
PQReadiness_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where AssetKind == "tls-config"
| where QuantumPosture in ("vulnerable", "partial")
| where Metadata contains "TLSv1.0" or Metadata contains "TLSv1.1" or Metadata contains "TLSv1.2"
| project TimeGenerated, ResourceName, ResourceType, AssetIdentifier, PostureReason, RiskScore, SubscriptionId, ResourceGroup
| order by RiskScore desc

properties.displayName: Internal endpoint using TLS protocol below 1.3

properties.description:
A network appliance or internal Azure endpoint with quantum-vulnerable posture appeared that
was not observed in the previous 24-hour scan cycle. This may indicate a new deployment, a
configuration change, or a newly discovered endpoint that should have been provisioned with
PQ-hybrid cryptography.
properties.displayName: New quantum-vulnerable appliance or internal resource appeared
properties.query:
let previous = PQReadiness_CL
  | where TimeGenerated between (ago(2d) .. ago(1d))
  | where QuantumPosture == "vulnerable"
  | distinct AssetIdentifier;
PQReadiness_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where QuantumPosture == "vulnerable"
| where AssetIdentifier !in (previous)
| project TimeGenerated, ResourceName, ResourceType, AssetIdentifier, AssetKind, Algorithm, PostureReason, RiskScore, SubscriptionId, ResourceGroup

properties.displayName: New quantum-vulnerable appliance or internal resource appeared

properties.description: AppliancePQCReadyDetected_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.0.0

A network appliance has been confirmed as post-quantum ready. This may indicate a QCrypton PQC
Engine deployment on F5 BIG-IP, a hybrid key exchange (X25519MLKEM768) negotiation, or an
ML-DSA/ML-KEM certificate in use. This is a positive signal — the appliance is protected against
harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks.
properties.displayName: PQC-ready appliance detected — quantum-safe posture confirmed
properties.query:
PQReadiness_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where QuantumPosture == "compliant"
| where Metadata contains "pqc_hybrid_key_exchange"
    or Metadata contains "f5_pqc_engine_active"
    or Metadata contains "f5_cert_pqc_ready"
    or Metadata contains "pqc_cert_ready"
| project TimeGenerated, ResourceName, ResourceType, AssetIdentifier, Algorithm, PostureReason, SubscriptionId, ResourceGroup

properties.displayName: PQC-ready appliance detected — quantum-safe posture confirmed

properties.description: HighRiskInternalEndpoint_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.0.0

An internal endpoint or network appliance has a risk score above 20, indicating critical or high
severity quantum vulnerabilities. This may include expired certificates on appliances, RSA keys
shorter than 2048 bits, or multiple compounding vulnerabilities on the same endpoint. Immediate
remediation is recommended.
properties.displayName: High-risk internal endpoint with critical quantum vulnerability
properties.query:
PQReadiness_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where QuantumPosture == "vulnerable"
| where RiskScore > 20
| project TimeGenerated, ResourceName, ResourceType, AssetIdentifier, AssetKind, Algorithm, KeySize, SignatureAlgorithm, PostureReason, RiskScore, ExpiresOn, SubscriptionId, ResourceGroup
| order by RiskScore desc

properties.displayName: High-risk internal endpoint with critical quantum vulnerability

properties.description: ApplianceCertExpiringSoon_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.0.0

A network appliance TLS certificate is expiring within the next 30 days and uses a classical
(quantum-vulnerable) signature algorithm. Certificate renewal is an ideal time to migrate to a
PQ-hybrid certificate. If the certificate is renewed with a classical algorithm, the
harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure window resets for the new validity period.
properties.displayName: Appliance certificate expiring within 30 days with classical algorithm
properties.query:
PQReadiness_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where AssetKind == "tls-cert"
| where QuantumPosture == "vulnerable"
| where isnotnull(ExpiresOn) and ExpiresOn between (now() .. ago(-30d))
| where ResourceType has_any ("F5", "CheckPoint", "PaloAlto", "Cisco", "Fortinet")
    or Metadata contains "certificate_expiring"
| project TimeGenerated, ResourceName, ResourceType, AssetIdentifier, SignatureAlgorithm, ExpiresOn, RiskScore, PostureReason, SubscriptionId, ResourceGroup
| order by ExpiresOn asc

properties.displayName: Appliance certificate expiring within 30 days with classical algorithm
